issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Meal differs between the problem statement/solution and the template. The problem statement's UML (and the solution implementation) specify Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) — name first, ingredients second. The template's Meal.java defines the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) — ingredients first, name second. This mismatch will confuse students and can cause code that assumes the UML/solution ordering (for example the example calls in Main) to fail to compile or behave incorrectly.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template constructor with the problem statement and solution by changing the constructor signature in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java to: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) { ... }. Update any example calls in Main (if uncommented) to match this ordering. Alternatively, if the intent was to have the reversed order, update the problem statement UML to reflect the template; however, keeping the constructor as (String name, String[] ingredients) is recommended to match the provided solution and UML.
